# dsh-proactive · the night watchman

> A DSH plugin that lets the agent **speak up on its own** when a long job finishes
> after its turn
has already ended — no more coming back to ask "is it done yet?".
中文说明 →
## What it does

You ask the agent to do something that takes hours — pull down a 40 GB model, wait for a
compile, si

t through an installer. The agent starts the job, the turn ends, and it goes to
sleep. The job is st

ill running. **Nothing tells the agent when it finishes**, so nothing
tells you either: you have to
wander back and ask.

This plugin makes DSH watch the condition for you. When it is met, the plugin injects one
message in
to the session and wakes the agent — so the agent reports to you by itself.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Why it exists

An agent is a request/response process. Once a turn is over it has no clock, no timer and no
way to

learn that a `curl` it launched has exited or that a file has appeared on disk. Under
DSH the only t

hing that can hand it that fact is a message arriving in its inbox — which is
exactly what a session

looks like when *you* type something. If nothing sends one, the agent
stays asleep until a human po

like when *you* type something. If nothing sends one, the agent
stays asleep until a human pokes it.

So the missing piece is not the waiting, it is the *waking*. This plugin is the thing that
wakes it.
## Mechanics

The wake-up uses the same call DSH itself uses when a subagent reports back to its parent
agent (see
`dsh-subagent/lib/continuation.js`):
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`agent.steer(...)` is the door into a session that is not currently running a turn;
`createUserMessa

ge(...)` builds the message object that door expects. This is DSH's own API
surface, not a private b

lds the message object that door expects. This is DSH's own API
surface, not a private back channel.

`source.kind = 'plugin'` is the default, and it matters: a plugin-originated message **is not
render

ed in the UI**. You do not see a fake bubble pretending to be something you typed —
you only see the

agent's reply, which is the whole point. `source.kind = 'user'` is available
per-entry if you delib

erately want the message rendered as a user bubble, and it is used by
the test suite to prove the di

message rendered as a user bubble, and it is used by
the test suite to prove the difference is real.
## Trigger types
| `type` | Fires when | Required fields |
| `file-stable` | The file size is unchanged across `rounds` consecutive checks — **the standard "do

wnload finished" test** | `path`, `rounds` (default `stableRounds`, 3) |
| `file-exists` | The path

exists **as a file** (a directory does not count) | `path` |
| `file-size` | The file exists and its

size is ≥ `bytes` | `path`, `bytes` (default 0) |
| `process-exit` | The named process is gone — **

the job it was doing is over** | `process` (e.g. `curl.exe`) |
| `port-open` | A TCP connection to `

host:port` succeeds — **the service came up** | `port`, `host` (default `127.0.0.1`) |
| `time` | Th
e clock passes `at` — an alarm | `at` (ISO date-time; bare = local, `Z` = UTC) |
Unknown types never fire; they are skipped silently rather than guessed at.
## Requirements / compatibility

**After installing, confirm it actually works — a profile that boots is not proof.**
A plugin can lo

ad cleanly, serve its routes and still break the host; we have seen exactly
that. So the acceptance

test is: **create a new session and send it one message** (the plugin
is idle until a watch fires, s

o a quiet log is expected), then confirm the session exists and
the agent answered. If new sessions

cannot be created at all, remove the mount line above and
restart.

Developed and tested against DSH **`0.1.0-rc.7`** — a **customised** build, not a stock
upstream rel

ease. Another version may register its services or name its events differently:
this plugin uses `ct

x.on`, `ctx.effect`, `ctx.agents`, the `agent/created`,
`agent/session-start`, `agent/inbox/inserted

`, `agent/status` and `agent/disposed` events, and
`agent.steer` + `createUserMessage` from `@deepse

s` and `agent/disposed` events, and
`agent.steer` + `createUserMessage` from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm`.

If your build does not match, the plugin **deactivates and says so** — it does **not** stop the
prof

ile from booting. Nothing keeps running (no listeners, no timer), and `boot.log` gets ONE
line inste
ad of the ready line:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

**If the profile will not start at all after installing**, remove the mounted lines from
`<profile>/

cordis.patch.yml` (or drop `"dsh-proactive"` from `dsh.profile.bundles`, if that is
how you installe

(or drop `"dsh-proactive"` from `dsh.profile.bundles`, if that is
how you installed it) and restart:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Known limitations

- **The bare-timer fallback is gone (Unreleased).** Up to 0.2.1, a failing `ctx.effect` fell
back to

a plain `setInterval` that lived until the process exited. That fallback was removed:
a plugin that

cannot register is now deactivated with one line in `boot.log`, so a plugin
instance can always be

fully unloaded.
- **`watch.json` is module-level state.** The path is shared across `apply()` calls

in one
process, so two loaded instances would fight over it. Fine for one plugin per DSH process —
w

hich is the supported shape.
- **`file-exists` ignores directories** on purpose: "the directory exis

ts" is not the same
claim as "the download finished".
- **`process-exit` relies on `tasklist` on Win

dows.** Where the process lookup fails, the
condition reports "unknown" and the entry is skipped for

that tick instead of firing — a
missing `tasklist` cannot cause a false positive.
- **`file-stable`

detects "size stopped changing", not "transfer completed"** — a stalled
download looks identical to

a finished one. Use `file-size` with a known expected size when
it matters.
- **Watching is poll-ba

sed.** With `intervalMs: 15000` a condition can be met up to one
interval before the agent is woken.
Shorter intervals cost CPU; the floor is 3000 ms.
